Shows the celestial body you are 
scanning and the active scan mode. 
Drag the targeting reticle for 
information about a specific location 
or to place a waypoint there.

Shows information about where the 
map is on the celestial body and 
more specific data about the targeted 
location.
Places a waypoint where your \ntargeting reticle is located using the \nname in the text box just above it.
The interface to KerbNet is called up from the Action menu on KerbNet scanners.
Fades some items on the map so that \nyou can see the data more clearly.
Cycles through KerbNet's specified \nautomatic refresh intervals.
Make a fresh scan below your vessel.

Available on highly specialized 
KerbNet scanners. It allows you to 
view detailed scans of the resource 
concentrations on a celestial body 
in contrasting color schemes. 

This makes it much easier to 
decide where to set up your 
mining bases.

Basic monochromatic scan of the 
terrain heights of the celestial 
body. Placing the targeting reticle 
will show you the height at any 
given location. 

It is available on most KerbNet 
scanners and is useful for locating 
safe landing sites.

Available on more advanced 
KerbNet scanners. It allows you to 
see a colorful biome map of the 
celestial body below you. 

This allows you to optimize your 
hopping from biome to biome.
KerbNet has three modes of operation -- depending on the scanners capabilities.

Sometimes a scan will pick up something truly unexpected, and 
your scientists will mark this with a question mark. 

These anomalous readings may disappear and reappear 
sporadically, so it is suggested that you tag them with a waypoint 
for future investigation.

Every scan mode in KerbNet allows you to place 
custom named waypoints on the map by moving 
the targeting reticle to a location and clicking the 
waypoint button. 

You can easily navigate to these waypoints by 
clicking them in map view.

Warp Action: Select what should happen to timewarp as the alarm is approached.
Message: Select messaging to give when the alarm is triggered.
Options: Toggle alarm sound and automatic alarm deletion.
Several different types of alarms can be created.  Note that some require a vessel to be selected.
Use these to help keep track of the purpose of this alarm.
A list of the available alarm types. Some examples below.
Start of a transfer window to a particular CB.
Specific settings that vary per alarm type.
Specific spots on a craft’s orbital path.
Linked to a specific craft’s maneuver.
User defined timing for any purpose.

The alarm clock allows you to set alarms for events you don’t want to miss.  This can alert you to events like upcoming maneuvers on vessels, transfer windows , or any time you choose to set a reminder.
After selecting an alarm you can click these buttons to Edit the alarm, Switch To the vessel the alarm pertains to, or Warp To the alarm time.
